sanskrit: apa prāca indra viśvām̐ amitrān apāpāco abhibhūte nudasva | apodīco apa śūrādharāca urau yathā tava śarman madema ||
english: Drive away from us, O Indra, O conqueror, all enemies toward the east, drive them toward the west; drive them toward the north, drive the mighty ones downward, that we may rejoice in thy broad shelter.

sanskrit: kuvid aṅga yavamanto yavaṁ cid yathā dānty anupūrvaṁ viyūya | iheha iṣāṁ kṛṇuhi bhojanāni ye barhiṣo namovṛktiṁ na jagmuḥ ||
english: Do those who have barley indeed thresh the barley in order, one after another? Make the enjoyments of those here and here [for us], who have not come [merely] to bend the knee at the sacred grass.

sanskrit: nahi sthūry ṛtuthā yātam asti nota śravo vivide saṁgameṣu | gavyanta indraṁ sakhyāya viprā aśvāyanto vṛṣaṇaṁ vājayantaḥ ||
english: Not by the proper season is the [fitting] time of your coming, nor has renown been found in assemblies — the inspired poets, desiring cattle, desiring horses, seeking the stallion Indra for friendship.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ surāmam aśvinā namucāv āsure sacā | vipipānā śubhas patī indraṁ karmasv āvatam ||
english: You two Aśvins, while drinking the surā with the Asura Namuci, O lords of splendour, having drunk deeply, helped Indra in his deeds.

sanskrit: putram iva pitarāv aśvinobhendrāvathuḥ kāvyair daṁsanābhiḥ | yat surāmaṁ vy apibaḥ śacībhiḥ sarasvatī tvā maghavann abhiṣṇak ||
english: Like two parents [guarding] a son, you two Aśvins aided Indra with your wisdom and wondrous powers. When thou drankest the surā in full with thy might, Sarasvatī, O bountiful one, sprinkled thee.

sanskrit: indraḥ sutrāmā svavām̐ avobhiḥ sumṛḻīko bhavatu viśvavedāḥ | bādhatāṁ dveṣo abhayanṁ kṛṇotu suvīryasya patayaḥ syāma ||
english: May Indra, the good protector, self-sufficient with his aids, all-knowing, be gracious to us. May he thrust back enmity, make us fearless — may we be lords of heroic vigour.

sanskrit: tasya vayaṁ sumatau yajñiyasyāpi bhadre saumanase syāma | sa sutrāmā svavām̐ indro asme ārāc cid dveṣaḥ sanutar yuyotu ||
english: May we be in the good favour and the blessed benevolence of that worshipful one. May that Indra, the good protector, self-sufficient, drive enmity far away from us, even from afar.

sanskrit: ījānam id dyaur gūrtāvasur ījānam bhūmir abhi prabhūṣaṇi | ījānaṁ devāv aśvināv abhi sumnair avardhatām ||
english: Heaven, rich in good treasure, blessed the sacrificer; Earth, the abundant bestower, [blessed] the sacrificer. The two divine Aśvins caused the sacrificer to thrive with their favours.

sanskrit: tā vām mitrāvaruṇā dhārayatkṣitī suṣumneṣitatvatā yajāmasi | yuvoḥ krāṇāya sakhyair abhi ṣyāma rakṣasaḥ ||
english: You two, O Mitra and Varuṇa, supporters of the settlements, we worship, urged on by your great favour. May we, through friendship with you twain, be beyond the reach of demons.

sanskrit: adhā cin nu yad didhiṣāmahe vām abhi priyaṁ rekṇaḥ patya māṇāḥ | dadvām̐ vā yat puṣyati rekṇaḥ sam v āran nakir asya maghāni ||
english: Even now, as we strive toward you with the dear wealth that we cherish — or as the wealth he has given thrives — none [can] dispute his bounties.

sanskrit: asāv anyo asura sūyata dyaus tvaṁ viśveṣāṁ varuṇāsi rājā | mūrdhā rathasya cākan naitāvatainas āntakadhruk ||
english: That other [sky] was born as a heaven, O Asura; thou, O Varuṇa, art king of all. The head of the chariot so chosen — not so great a guilt does a sin-destroyer [demand].

sanskrit: asmin sv etac chakapūta eno hite mitre nigatān hanti vīrān | avor vā yad dhāt tanūṣv avaḥ priyāsu yajñiyāsv arvā ||
english: In this [friend], truly, O Śakapūta, this guilt [lies]: one kills the heroes who are bound in Mitra held fast. Or what benefit he established in their own bodies, in those dear to them and sacred to the sacrifice.

sanskrit: yuvor hi mātāditir vicetasā dyaur na bhūmiḥ payasā pupūtani | ava priyā didiṣṭana sūro ninikta raśmibhiḥ ||
english: For Aditi, your mother, all-wise, has purified [you both] with her milk, like Heaven or like Earth. [Now] shine down, beloved ones; the Sun has anointed [you] with his rays.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ hy apnarājāv asīdataṁ tiṣṭhad rathaṁ na dhūrṣadaṁ vanaṛṣadam | tā naḥ kaṇūkayantīr nṛmedhas tatre aṁhasaḥ sumedhas tatre aṁhasaḥ ||
english: For you two, kings of possession, were seated in the standing chariot, resting on the shaft, sitting in the forest. May those [helpers], roaring for us — Nṛmedhas saved us from trouble; Sumedhas saved from trouble.

sanskrit: pro ṣv asmai purora tham indrāya śūṣam arcata | abhīke cid u lokakṛt saṁge samatsu vṛtrahā asmākam bodhi coditā nabha ntām anyakeṣāṁ jyākā adhi dhanvasu ||
english: Sing forth a mighty [hymn] to Indra, with the pūroratham [verse] first. Even in close combat a world-maker, in encounters and in battles a slayer of Vṛtra — be our inciter. May the bowstrings of the others snap on their bows.

sanskrit: tvaṁ sindhūm̐r avāsṛjo adharāco ahann ahim | aśatrur indra jajñiṣe viśvam puṣyasi vāryaṁ taṁ tvā pari ṣvajāmahe nabha ntām anyakeṣāṁ jyākā adhi dhanvasu ||
english: Thou didst release the rivers flowing downward, thou didst slay the serpent. O Indra, thou wast born without enemies; thou dost nourish all that is desirable — thee we embrace. May the bowstrings of the others snap on their bows.

sanskrit: vi ṣu viśvā arātayo aryo naśanta no dhiyaḥ | astāsi śatrave vadhaṁ yo na indra jighāṁsati yā te rātir dadir vasu nabha ntām anyakeṣāṁ jyākā adhi dhanvasu ||
english: May all the hostile ones perish; may those of the enemy not harm our prayers. Thou art the hurler of the slaying bolt against the foe who would kill us, O Indra; thy bounty gives wealth. May the bowstrings of the others snap on their bows.

sanskrit: yo na indrābhito jano vṛkāyur ādideśati | adhaspadaṁ tam īṁ kṛdhi vibādho asi sāsahir nabha ntām anyakeṣāṁ jyākā adhi dhanvasu ||
english: Whoever of the people around us, O Indra, points out [the way] with the eye of a wolf — bring him down low; thou art the repeller, the conqueror. May the bowstrings of the others snap on their bows.

sanskrit: yo na indrābhidāsati sanābhir yaś ca niṣṭyaḥ | ava tasya balaṁ tira mahīva dyaur adha tmanā nabha ntām anyakeṣāṁ jyākā adhi dhanvasu ||
english: Whoever harms us, O Indra, whether he be of our own kin or a stranger — overcome his strength, as great Heaven does by its own power. May the bowstrings of the others snap on their bows.

sanskrit: vayam indra tvāyavaḥ sakhitvam ā rabhāmahe | ṛtasya naḥ pathā nayāti viśvāni duritā nabha ntām anyakeṣāṁ jyākā adhi dhanvasu ||
english: We, O Indra, yearning for thee, take hold of friendship. May he lead us by the path of Ṛta beyond all evils. May the bowstrings of the others snap on their bows.

sanskrit: asmabhyaṁ su tvam indra tāṁ śikṣa yā dohate prati varaṁ jaritre | acchidrodhnī pīpayad yathā naḥ sahasradhārā payasā mahī gauḥ ||
english: Do thou, O Indra, generously grant us that [cow] who yields according to the wish of the praiser — may the great cow with a thousand streams, with unbroken udder, pour milk upon us.

sanskrit: ubhe yad indra rodasī āpaprāthoṣā iva | mahāntaṁ tvā mahīnāṁ samrājaṁ carṣaṇīnāṁ devī janitrī ajījanad bhadrā janitrī ajījanat ||
english: When thou, O Indra, didst fill both the world-halves, like the Dawn — the divine mother brought thee forth, great, emperor of the great ones, sovereign of the peoples; the auspicious mother brought thee forth.

sanskrit: ava sma durhaṇāyato martasya tanuhi sthiram | adhaspadaṁ tam īṁ kṛdhi yo asmām̐ ādideśati devī janitrī ajījanad bhadrā janitrī ajījanat ||
english: Pierce through the stubborn [body] of the mortal who is ill-intentioned toward us; bring low him who points [enemies] at us — the divine mother brought thee forth, the auspicious mother brought thee forth.

sanskrit: ava tyā bṛhatīr iṣo viśvaścandrā amitrahan | śacībhiḥ śakra dhūnuhīndra viśvābhir ūtibhir devī janitrī ajījanad bhadrā janitrī ajījanat ||
english: Shake down those great refreshments, bright as all things, O slayer of enemies; with thy powers, O Śakra, O Indra, with all thy aids — the divine mother brought thee forth, the auspicious mother brought thee forth.

sanskrit: ava yat tvaṁ śatakratav indra viśvāni dhūṇuṣe | rayiṁ na sunvate sacā sahasriṇībhir ūtibhir devī janitrī ajījanad bhadrā janitrī ajījanat ||
english: When thou, O Indra of a hundred powers, shakest all things down, together with riches for the soma-presser, with a thousandfold of aids — the divine mother brought thee forth, the auspicious mother brought thee forth.

sanskrit: ava svedā ivābhito viṣvak patantu didyavaḥ | dūrvāyā iva tantavo vy asmad etu durmatiḥ devī janitrī ajījanad bhadrā janitrī ajījanat ||
english: Let the missiles fall in all directions around like drops of sweat; may ill-will depart from us like the threads of the dūrvā grass — the divine mother brought thee forth, the auspicious mother brought thee forth.

sanskrit: dīrghaṁ hy aṅkuśaṁ yathā śaktim bibharṣi mantumaḥ | pūrveṇa maghavan padā ajo vayāṁ yathā yamo devī janitrī ajījanad bhadrā janitrī ajījanat ||
english: For thou bearest the goad like a long hook, O thoughtful one; with thy former step, O bountiful one, thou dost direct the people like Yama — the divine mother brought thee forth, the auspicious mother brought thee forth.

sanskrit: nakir devā minīmasi nakir ā yopayāmasi mantraśrutyaṁ carāmasi | pakṣebhir apikakṣebhir atrābhi saṁ rabhāmahe ||
english: We do not injure the gods; we do not obstruct [their worship]; we walk [the path of] obedience to the sacred word. Here, with wings and with embracing arms, we together take hold [of you].

sanskrit: yasmin vṛkṣe supalāśe devaiḥ sampibate yamaḥ | atrā no viśpatiḥ pitā purāṇām̐ anu venati ||
english: In the tree with beautiful leaves where Yama drinks with the gods — there our father, the lord of the dwelling, delights in the ancient ones.

sanskrit: purāṇām̐ anuvena ntaṁ carantam pāpayāmu yā | asūyann abhy acākaśaṁ tasmā aspṛhayam punaḥ ||
english: I gazed after him, the one who follows after the ancient ones, walking along the evil path; grieving, I yearned for him once more.

sanskrit: yaṁ kumāra navaṁ ratham acakram manasā kṛṇoḥ | ekeṣaṁ viśvataḥ prāñcam apaśyann adhi tiṣṭhasi ||
english: The new chariot without wheels which thou, O boy, didst fashion in thy mind — it has but a single shaft, facing all sides: thou climbest upon it unseen.

sanskrit: yaṁ kumāra prāvartayo rathaṁ viprebhyas pari | taṁ sāmānu prāvartata sam ito nāvy āhitam ||
english: The chariot thou, O boy, didst set rolling beyond the wise sages — that [chariot] rolled on together with [the hymn]; a boat was set on [the voyage].

sanskrit: kaḥ kumāram ajanayad rathaṁ ko nir avartayat | kaḥ svit tad adya no brūyād anudeyī yathābhavat ||
english: Who begat the boy? Who set the chariot rolling? Who could today tell us how the gift-for-the-dead came to be?

sanskrit: yathābhavad anudeyī tato agra ajāyata | purastād budhna ātataḥ paścān nirayaṇaṁ kṛtam ||
english: As the gift-for-the-dead came to be, from that the beginning was born. The foundation was spread out in front; behind, the exit was made.

sanskrit: idaṁ yamasya sādanaṁ devamānaṁ yad ucyate | iyam asya dhamyate nāḻīr ayaṁ gīrbhiḥ pariṣkṛtaḥ ||
english: This dwelling of Yama, which is called the god-built hall — here his flute is blown, here he is adorned with songs.

sanskrit: keśy agniṁ keśī viṣaṁ keśī bibharti rodasī | keśī viśvaṁ svar dṛśe keśīdaṁ jyotir ucyate ||
english: The Keśin bears fire; the Keśin bears poison; the Keśin bears heaven and earth. The Keśin bears all to behold the sun; the Keśin is called this light.

sanskrit: munayo vātaraśanāḥ piśaṅgā vasate malā | vātasyānu dhrājiṁ yanti yad devāso avikṣata ||
english: The munis are girdled with the wind; they wear soiled [garments] of yellowish-brown hue. They follow the rushing course of the wind, wherever the gods have vanished.

sanskrit: unmad itā mauneyena vātām̐ ā tasthimā vayam | śarīred asmākaṁ yūyam martāso abhi paśyatha ||
english: Exhilarated by the state of the muni, we have mounted the wind. You mortals behold only our bodies.

sanskrit: antarikṣeṇa patati viśvā rūpāvacākaśat | muniḥ devasya-devasya saukṛtyāya sakhā hitaḥ ||
english: He flies through the mid-air; he has seen all forms. The muni is the friend placed [as companion] for the good work of every god and every god.

sanskrit: vātasyāśvo vāyoḥ sakhā tho deveṣito muniḥ | ubhau samudrāv ā kṣeti yaś ca pūrva utāparaḥ ||
english: The steed of the wind, the companion of Vāyu — the muni is impelled by the gods. He dwells upon both oceans, the eastern and the western.

sanskrit: apsarasāṁ gandharvāṇām mṛgāṇāṁ caraṇe caran | keśī ketasya vidvān sakhā svādur madintamaḥ ||
english: Roaming in the footsteps of the Apsarasas, the Gandharvas, and the beasts — the Keśin, knowing [all] intentions, is the sweetest and most intoxicating friend.

sanskrit: vāyur asmā upāmanthat pinaṣṭi smā kunanna mā | keśī viṣasya pātreṇa yad rudreṇāpibat saha ||
english: Vāyu churned [the drink] for him; Kunannamā pounded it. The Keśin drank from the cup of poison when he drank together with Rudra.

sanskrit: uta devā avahitaṁ devā un nayathā punaḥ | utāgaś cakruṣaṁ devā devā jīvayathā punaḥ ||
english: O gods, what is cast down, the gods lift up again. O gods, even one who has committed sin, the gods restore to life again.

sanskrit: dvāv imau vātau vāta ā sindhor ā parāvataḥ | dakṣaṁ te anya ā vātu parānyo vātu yad rapaḥ ||
english: These two winds blow, from the Sindhu and from the far distance. May one blow vigour to thee; may the other blow away whatever disease [there is].

sanskrit: ā vāta vāhi bheṣajaṁ vi vāta vāhi yad rapaḥ | tvaṁ hi viśvabheṣajo devānāṁ dūta īyase ||
english: Blow hither the healing, O Wind; blow away the disease, O Wind. For thou art the universal healer; thou movest as the messenger of the gods.

sanskrit: ā tvāgamaṁ śaṁtātibhir atho ariṣṭatātibhiḥ | dakṣaṁ te bhadram ābhārṣam parā yakṣmaṁ suvāmi te ||
english: I have come to thee with blessings, also with protections from harm. I have brought thee auspicious vigour; I drive away disease from thee.

sanskrit: trāyantām iha devās trāyatām marutāṁ gaṇaḥ | trāyantāṁ viśvā bhūtāni yathāyam arapā asat ||
english: May the gods protect him here; may the host of the Maruts protect him. May all beings protect him, so that he may be free from harm.

sanskrit: āpa id vā u bheṣajīr āpo amīvacātanīḥ | āpaḥ sarvasya bheṣajīs tās te kṛṇvantu bheṣajam ||
english: The Waters are indeed healers; the Waters dispel disease. The Waters are the remedy for all — may they work healing for thee.

sanskrit: hastābhyāṁ daśaśākhābhyāṁ jihvā vācaḥ purogavī | anāmayitnubhyāṁ tvā tābhyāṁ tvopa spṛśāmasi ||
english: With both hands, the ten-branched ones, and the tongue that leads speech — with those two free-from-disease [hands], we touch thee with them.

sanskrit: tava tya indra sakhyeṣu vahnaya ṛtam manvānā vy adardirur valam | yatrā daśasyann uṣaso riṇann apaḥ kutsāya manmano ahyaś ca daṁsayaḥ ||
english: Those bearers of oblation in thy friendships, O Indra, pondering the sacred order, burst Vala apart — where, honouring the Dawns and releasing the waters, [thou didst act] for Kutsa's praise, with thy wondrous deeds against the serpent.

sanskrit: avāsṛjaḥ prasvaḥ śvañcayo girīn ud āja usrā apibo madhu priyam | avardhayo vanino asya daṁsasā śuśoca sūrya ṛtajātayā girā ||
english: Thou didst release the springs; driving forward, thou didst push away the mountains; thou didst drive up the bright [cows], thou drankest the dear sweet drink. Thou didst magnify the forests with his wonder; the Sun blazed with the hymn born of sacred order.

sanskrit: vi sūryo madhye amucad rathaṁ divo vidad dāsāya pratimānam āryaḥ | dṛḻhāni pipror asurasya māyina indro vy āsyac cakṛvām̐ ṛjiśvanā ||
english: The Sun released his chariot in the mid-sky; the Ārya found a match for the Dāsa. The strongholds of Pipru the Asura, the deceiver — Indra burst them apart, acting together with Ṛjiśvan.

sanskrit: anādhṛṣṭāni dhṛṣito vy āsyan nidhīm̐r adevām̐ amṛṇad ayāsyaḥ ||māseva sūryo vasu puryam ā dade gṛṇānaḥ śatrūm̐r aśṛṇād virukmatā ||
english: The irresistible one violently burst apart the irresistible [things]; Ayāsya crushed the god-less hoards. Like the Sun [taking] the communal wealth of the month, being praised he shattered the enemies with his gleaming [power].

sanskrit: ayuddhaseno vibhvā vibhindatā dāśad vṛtrahā tujyāni tejate | indrasya vajrād abibhed abhiśnathaḥ prākrāmac chundhyūr ajahād uṣā anaḥ ||
english: Ayuddhasena, by the widespread [Indra] who cleaves, [the enemy] was granted [defeat]; the slayer of Vṛtra hones his sharp weapons. The crusher trembled at Indra's bolt; Śundhyu strode forth; the Dawn abandoned her car.

sanskrit: etā tyā te śrutyāni kevalā yad eka ekam akṛṇor ayajñam | māsāṁ vidhānam adadhā adhi dyavi tvayā vibhinnam bharati pradhi pitā ||
english: These are thy renowned [deeds], solely thine own, when one by one thou madest them offer no sacrifice. Thou didst place the ordering of the months in heaven; the father carries the wheel-rim split by thee.

sanskrit: sūryaraśmir harikeśaḥ purastāt savitā jyotir ud ayām̐ ajasram | tasya pūṣā prasave yāti vidvān sampaśyan viśvā bhuvanāni gopāḥ ||
english: Savitṛ with golden locks has raised up his light ceaselessly from the east. Pūṣan, knowing, goes forth at his impulse, the herdsman beholding all the worlds.

sanskrit: nṛcakṣā eṣa divo madhya āsta āpaprivān rodasī antarikṣam | sa viśvācīr abhi caṣṭe ghṛtācīr antarā pūrvam aparaṁ ca ketum ||
english: He, the beholder of men, stands in the mid-sky, having filled the two world-halves and the mid-air. He gazes all around at the luminous [regions], between the eastern and the western brightness.

sanskrit: rāyo budhnaḥ saṁgamano vasūnāṁ viśvā rūpābhi caṣṭe śacībhiḥ | deva iva savitā satyadharmendrona tasthau samare dhanānām ||
english: The foundation of wealth, the meeting-place of riches — he beholds all forms with his powers. Like the god Savitṛ of true ordinance, like Indra, he has not halted in the battle for treasures.

sanskrit: viśvāvasuṁ soma gandharvam āpo dadṛśuṣīs tad ṛtenā vy āyan | tad anvavaid indro rārahāṇa āsām pari sūryasya paridhīm̐r apaśyat ||
english: The Waters who had seen Viśvāvasu, the Gandharva, the Soma — they departed by sacred order. Indra, pleased, tracked them; he looked around at the enclosures of the Sun.

sanskrit: viśvāvasur abhi tan no gṛṇātu divyo gandharvो rajaso vimānaḥ | yad vā ghā satyam uta yan na vidma dhiyo hinvāno dhiya in no avyāḥ ||
english: May Viśvāvasu, the heavenly Gandharva who measures out the firmament, sing that for us. Whether it be the truth, or whether we know it not — may he, spurring our thoughts, protect our thoughts.

sanskrit: sasnim avindat caraṇe nadīnām apāvṛṇod duro aśmavrajānām | prāsāṁ gandharvो amṛtāni vocad indro dakṣaṁ pari jānād ahīnām ||
english: He found the winning one at the course of the rivers; he opened the doors of the rocky enclosures. The Gandharva declared the immortal [words] to them; Indra came to know the power of the serpents.

sanskrit: agne tava śravo vayo mahi bhrājante arcayo vibhāvaso | bṛhadbhāno śavasā vājam ukthyaṁ dadhāsi dāśuṣe kave ||
english: O Agni, great is thy fame; thy flames blaze, O Vibhāvasu. O Bṛhadbhānu, with thy might thou bestowest the prize worth hymning upon the worshipping sage.

sanskrit: pāvakavarcāḥ śukravarcā anūnavarcā ud iyarṣi bhānunā | putro mātarā vicarann upāvasi pṛṇakṣi rodasī ubhe ||
english: With purifying splendour, with bright splendour, with undiminished splendour thou risest with thy light. Moving about as a son [between] his two mothers, thou dost approach and fill both Heaven and Earth.

sanskrit: ūrjo napāj jātavedaḥ suśastibhir mandasva dhītibhir hitaḥ | tve iṣaḥ saṁ dadhur bhūrivarpasaś citraotayo vāmajātāḥ ||
english: O grandson of Strength, O Jātavedas, rejoice with our fair praises, gladdened by [our] devotions. In thee the many-formed ones, of various refreshments, born of bounty, have gathered together their impulses.

sanskrit: irajyann agne prathayasva jantubhir asme rāyo amartya | sa darśatasya vapuṣo vi rājasi pṛṇakṣi sānasiṁ kratum ||
english: Ruling, O Agni, O immortal, spread thyself widely through living beings among us as [bringer of] wealth. Thou shinest with radiant form; thou dost fill the winning purpose [with vigour].

sanskrit: iṣkartāram adhvarasya pracetasaṁ kṣayantaṁ rādhasō mahaḥ | rātiṁ vāmasya subhagāṁ mahīm iṣaṁ dadhāsi sānasiṁ rayim ||
english: Thou bestowest the great, auspicious gift of bounty and impulse with winning wealth — thou, the all-wise performer of the sacrifice, the sovereign of great munificence.

sanskrit: ṛtāvānam mahiṣaṁ viśvadarśatam agniṁ sumnāya dadhire puro janāḥ | śrutkarṇaṁ saprathastamaṁ tvā girā daivyam mānuṣā yugā ||
english: Men have placed Agni foremost for [their] welfare — the great bull, obedient to sacred order, visible to all, the one who hears [prayer]. With song, O divine one, the generations of men [praise] thee, the most widely renowned, whose ear is open.
